title.ja: 図1-1 相手玉が詰んでいる例
title.en: Figure 1-1: Example of a checkmated opposing king

explain.ja: 詰みとは、相手玉がどんな手を指しても次に取られてしまう状態で、将棋はこの状態を目指すゲームです。ただしいきなり詰ますことはできないため、まず敵陣に攻め駒を配置します。「4枚の攻めは切れない」という格言のとおり、敵陣の玉の近くに4枚ほど駒があれば攻め駒として十分です。わかりやすい形は、飛車と角を敵陣に成り込んで龍と馬を作り、敵陣の桂馬と香車を取って持ち駒にして打ち込み、龍・馬・桂・香の4枚で攻めるものです。攻めの4ステップは、飛車や角を成り込む、龍や馬で桂香などを取る、持ち駒を打って4枚以上で攻める、最後に詰ます、です。守りは基本的に攻めの逆で、相手の飛車角の成り込みや持ち駒の増加を防ぎ、自玉の詰みを避けます。
explain.en: Checkmate means the opponent's king is captured next whatever they play, and shogi is the game of aiming for it. You cannot mate immediately, so first place attacking pieces in the enemy camp. By the proverb "a four-piece attack doesn't break", about four of your pieces near the enemy king are enough attackers. A clear pattern is to promote the rook and bishop in the enemy camp into dragon and horse, capture the enemy knight and lance and drop them as pieces in hand, attacking with dragon, horse, knight and lance. The four attack steps: promote rook/bishop in the enemy camp, capture knights and lances with them, drop pieces in hand to attack with four or more pieces, then mate. Defence is basically the reverse: prevent the opponent's rook and bishop from promoting, deny them pieces in hand, and avoid your own mate.

explain.ja: 図2-1は将棋の初期配置です。先ほど述べたように、まず飛車や角を敵陣に成り込むことを狙うので、初手は▲3四歩ではなく角や飛車の道を開ける▲7六歩や▲2六歩のような手がよいでしょう。
explain.en: Figure 2-1 is the starting position. As explained, the aim is first to promote the rook or bishop in the enemy camp, so the first move should open the way for the bishop or rook, such as ▲7六歩 or ▲2六歩.

section.ja: 序盤は飛車や角を活用していく
section.en: In the opening, make use of the rook and bishop

title.ja: 図2-2 初手▲3四歩で角を使う
title.en: Figure 2-2: First move ▲3四歩 uses the bishop

explain.ja: まず飛車や角を敵陣に成り込むことを狙うため、初手は角や飛車が動けるように道を開ける手がよいでしょう。▲3四歩や▲2六歩がその例です。
explain.en: Since the first aim is to promote the rook or bishop in the enemy camp, the opening move should open a path for them. ▲3四歩 and ▲2六歩 are examples.

section.ja: 序盤は飛車や角を活用していく
section.en: In the opening, make use of the rook and bishop

title.ja: 図2-3 初手▲2六歩で飛車を使う
title.en: Figure 2-3: First move ▲2六歩 uses the rook

explain.ja: 序盤の基本方針は、さらに飛車の前の歩をどんどん突いて、飛車を敵陣に成り込むことを目指すことです。お互いの駒がぶつかって取り合う展開になれば中盤の入り口で、中盤では駒得を狙いながら飛車の成り込みを目指します。
explain.en: The basic opening plan is to keep advancing the pawn in front of the rook and aim to promote the rook in the enemy camp. When the pieces collide and captures begin, the middlegame starts, in which you aim for material gain while heading for a rook promotion.

section.ja: 序盤は飛車や角を活用していく
section.en: In the opening, make use of the rook and bishop

title.ja: 図2-4 お互いに歩を持っている
title.en: Figure 2-4: Both sides have a pawn in hand

explain.ja: この状態では、お互いに歩を1枚ずつ持っています。ここから数手進めて、先手と後手の持ち駒に注目します。
explain.en: Both sides hold one pawn here. Advance a few moves and watch the pieces in hand of Black and White.

section.en: Aim to gain material in the middlegame

title.ja: 図2-5 先手は相手の角を取った
title.en: Figure 2-5: Black captured the opponent's bishop

explain.ja: まず先手は香車を前に進めて相手の角を取りました。さらに1手進めます。
explain.en: First, Black advances the lance and captures the opponent's bishop. Play one more move.

section.en: Aim to gain material in the middlegame

title.ja: 図2-6 後手は香車を取った

explain.ja: 後手も香車を進めて先手の香車を取り返します。持ち駒を見ると、先手は角、後手は香車が増えています。先手から見れば香車を渡して角を得たので、香車と角の交換です。角は香車より動ける範囲が広く価値が高いので、先手は得をしました。このようにトータルで価値の高い駒を得ることを「駒得」と言います。中盤で駒がぶつかったら駒得できる指し方を心がけましょう。
explain.en: White also advances a lance and recaptures Black's lance. Black's pieces in hand now include a bishop and White's a lance. From Black's side a lance was given up for a bishop, an exchange of lance for bishop; the bishop has a wider range and is worth more, so Black comes out ahead. Gaining the more valuable piece overall is called koma-doku (piece gain). When pieces collide in the middlegame, aim to gain material.

section.en: Aim to gain material in the middlegame

title.en: Figure 2-7: Partial diagram of the endgame

explain.ja: 図2-7を終盤の一部の局面と考えてください。ここではどう指すのがよいでしょうか。駒を取り合う段階になったら、価値の高い駒が取れるようにすればよいのです。
explain.en: Treat Figure 2-7 as part of an endgame position. How should one play here? Once pieces start being traded, aim to win the more valuable ones.

section.ja: 終盤は相手玉を詰ませる
section.en: In the endgame, checkmate the opponent's king

title.ja: 図2-8 飛車を捨ててしまう

explain.ja: ここでは▲2一飛成と金を取る手がよい手です。龍を取られて飛車と金の交換で駒損のようにも見えますが、さらに数手進めてみます。
explain.en: Here ▲2一飛成 capturing the gold is a good move. It may look like a material loss, trading a rook for a gold if the dragon is captured, but play a few more moves.

section.ja: 終盤は相手玉を詰ませる
section.en: In the endgame, checkmate the opponent's king

title.ja: 図2-9 駒損だが詰んでしまう
title.en: Figure 2-9: Down in material, but it is checkmate

explain.ja: △同玉と龍を取られたら、▲2二金と先ほど取った金を打てば相手玉は詰みます。玉の頭に金が打たれたこの詰みの形を「頭金」と呼びます。終盤では駒の損得より、いかに早く詰ますかを意識します。「終盤は駒得よりスピード」が大切で、詰みの形を覚えておくことが重要です。頭金の詰みを習得すれば初心者のうちは問題ありません。序盤は飛車や角を働かせ、中盤は駒得を狙いながら馬や龍を作り、終盤は駒得より詰ますスピードが大切です。
explain.en: If White captures the dragon with △同玉, dropping the captured gold with ▲2二金 mates the king. This mate shape, with a gold on the king's head, is called atamakin (頭金). In the endgame, think about how quickly you can mate rather than material; "speed over material in the endgame" matters, and memorising mating shapes is important. Mastering atamakin is enough for beginners. In short: use the rook and bishop well in the opening, make horse and dragon while winning material in the middlegame, and prioritise mating speed in the endgame.

section.ja: 終盤は相手玉を詰ませる
section.en: In the endgame, checkmate the opponent's king

title.ja: 図3-1 攻めと守りの陣形

explain.ja: 将棋の駒は攻めに向く駒と守りに向く駒があります。飛車・角は攻め、金将は守り、銀・桂・香は両方に使えます。「攻めは飛角銀桂」「玉の守りは金銀三枚」と言われ、よくある陣形は金2枚と銀1枚で玉を守り、飛車角と銀桂で攻める形です。図3-1の居角左美濃は攻めと守りの配置がきれいに分かれていて、右側に飛車・角・銀・桂の攻め駒、左側に金2枚と銀、さらに桂香で玉を守っています。
explain.en: Shogi pieces split into those suited to attack and those suited to defence. Rook and bishop are attackers, gold defends, and silver, knight and lance can do both. The sayings are "attack with rook, bishop, silver and knight" and "defend the king with three gold/silver"; a common setup guards the king with two golds and a silver and attacks with rook, bishop, silver and knight. Figure 3-1 is the Stationary Bishop Left Mino, where the attack and defence are cleanly separated: attackers (rook, bishop, silver, knight) on the right, and on the left two golds, a silver, plus knight and lance protecting the king.

section.en: How to balance attack and defense?
